page: Google Cloud Platform m3-ultramem-64 is a memory-optimized server instance designed for workloads requiring massive memory footprints relative to compute capacity. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 1952 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 30.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. Passmark database operations and CPU encryption tests also rank in the top 25%, demonstrating high efficiency for transactional and cryptographic workloads. Conversely, single-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, fall within the middle 50% average. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, also register in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers high memory density per vCPU, making it a specialized choice where memory capacity, rather than raw single-core compute speed, is the primary bottleneck. This resource profile is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, heavy data analytics pipelines, and memory-bound scientific simulations.
